reviews.text: My enjoyment is almost only due to the visceral experience of the entire nightmare playing out, and not from the meaning behind it.
reviews.author: Joseph Tomastik

reviews.text: This new horror starring Joaquin Phoenix and Patti LuPone is a building panic attack of a film - but its bloated, self-indulgent three-hour runtime lets it down.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: Terrific moments are ultimately stifled by Aster's disorganisation; he flits from the sublime to the downright stupid so often in Beau Is Afraid that it becomes impossible to guess whether each subsequent beat or moment will be a success or a disaster.
reviews.author: William Stottor

reviews.text: There is an evident consideration to theme, as is always the case with Aster, but the execution feels like it is having its cake and eating it too.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: Alas, at least the first hour of Beau is Afraid is a complete riot, a smorgasbord of black comedy and modern neuroses with a dash of slapstick. The real feat would have been to sustain that pace for the entire movie.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: “Beau Is Afraid” is a surreal Boots (“Sorry to Bother You”) Riley-esque “The Fabelmans” (2022) meets “The Truman Show” (1998) without being derivative and still delivering quintessential Aster cinema
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Aster continuously assaults your patience into something that never once materializes into anything tangible but is so riotously entertaining and absurd that you can’t help but love it.
reviews.author: Maxance Vincent

reviews.text: Our repressed fears and failure to confront our own demons will eventually find a way to reveal themselves. When they do, it can take the form of something positively absurd or darkly horrific.
reviews.author: Drew Tinnin

reviews.text: Beau is Afraid is a sprawling, rambling, picaresque story drenched in neurosis and packed with bizarre characters and encounters, all more or less functioning on an allegorical rather than literal level.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: The less you know about Beau is Afraid before going in, the better, because there's no movie as unique or surprising this year.
reviews.author: Danielle Ryan

reviews.text: Surreal expressionism of Ari Aster's Beau is Afraid--another director making a mark on me for the first time with a personal piece obsessed with the peculiarities and perversions of the life of the mind...
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Ostensibly Aster’s departure from horror, Beau Is Afraid might be the director’s scariest film yet.
reviews.author: Ella Feldman

reviews.text: It takes two hours and twenty minutes of Joaquin Phoenix's unadulterated exasperation, but [LuPone] does finally arrive to unsurprisingly be the best part of the whole even if her character is the catalyst for why it's all been so gosh darn boring.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: In his third film, Aster attempts to bewitch you with a pixel-perfect rendering of what feels like a three-hour panic attack that worsens every second.
reviews.author: Bhuvanesh Chandar

reviews.text: As a review, I don't know what to say. Outside of being a bit too long, most of the movie is a fever dream that made me giggle as times. I'll give it a B for being something very different.
reviews.author: Derek Sante

reviews.text: It shares DNA with movies like After Hours, Planes, Trains and Automobiles, and The Warriors but makes even the darkest moments in those pictures look like outtakes from The Oogieloves in the Big Balloon Adventure by comparison.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text:
[W]hile it is an impressive work from a bona fide auteur ... and a work of art that has blown away some of the smartest people in the industry, I scrawled a pithy note of my own while watching it. 

"Is this movie. Ever going to end?"
reviews.author: Jackson Weaver

reviews.text: These are not the lives any of us would want to live, or even dream about. But if surreal and absurd cinema has taught us anything, it’s that bad dreams often make good films.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: Playing with twisted dimensions and labyrinthine layers, Aster squanders the chance to lead a few good ideas to fruition. The result, much less fascinating than expected, is congested and appalling.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: An almost unclassifiable film, which loves to give its protagonist blow after hard blow. Even the occasional happy moment does not last long—they are all interrupted by moments of violence (physical or psychological) or pure chaos. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Though this isn't horror, it strives too hard to prove it is art. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hernán Ferreirós

reviews.text: A film I appreciate more for its artistic style & performances over how much I understood it.
reviews.author: Cris Parker

reviews.text: There is a decent amount of commitment to Beau Is Afraid given the length of running time, but it is well worth the watch.
reviews.author: June Butler

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is by far Ari Aster's most complex, inaccessible film to date, although guilt, extreme anxiety, and a complicated mother-son relationship are clear themes deeply explored throughout five sections.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Within Beau Is Afraid is a genuinely upsetting film about guilt, paranoia, and anxiety, but it’s so buried within its massive runtime that the weight of those themes is lost along the way. Beau may be afraid, but he’s also meandering & in need of editing
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Ari Aster’s gorgeous, amorphous epic is a mind-mutilating odyssey that can only be seen to be believed.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: A fever dream of uncomfortable proportions for anyone with a tinge of anxiety.  Ari Aster's ability to tap into an array of horrors that stem from our ill-programmed imbalance of how to live with ourselves is more unsettling than any ghoul, slasher or boo
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: An incredibly accurate depiction of Paranoia, anxiety, & the horrors of life. Phoenix is incredible, Patti LuPone is POWERFUL, but Ari Aster’s direction is something of a master. I loved almost all of it
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text:
A brilliant beginning is ruined by over-bloated middle part of the film with a load of unnecessary scenes. By the end you are praying for the credits to role.

It is saved though from it's creative opening and brilliant performance by Phoenix.
reviews.author: David Griffiths

reviews.text: Smart, dark, cerebral, gut-punching, hope-crushing, relatable, hilarious and horrific... it'd be the film's biggest surprise if Aster wasn't chuckling — and having the ultimate fever dream.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: The three-hour runtime and bananas tone will alienate many viewers. But if you’re into daring filmmaking, Aster doesn’t hold anything back.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: ...it is frightening, and at the same time equally fascinating.
reviews.author: Danny Minton

reviews.text: Beau is Afraid is an imaginative venture into the depths of Aster’s mind – a place where his fears, worries, anxieties, and pleasures come out to play.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is one of those impossible films that come by every once in a while that is worth watching for the risks it takes alone, for blatantly taking us to the bottom of its daring premise. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: Beau is Afraid takes a nose dive in its third act... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ezequiel Boetti

reviews.text: This twisted, neo-Homeric odyssey is maddening but oddly coherent in its intent: Telling the tragedy of a man whose umbilical cord has been repurposed as a leash.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: It’s hard to thrill to the turn of the screw when the wheels have already come off.
reviews.author: Ben Walters

reviews.text: Ari Aster amplifies the madness in his latest confined space thriller, but it is way too long, ambitious and exhausting.
reviews.author: Renuka Vyavahare

reviews.text: An often sensationally funny black comedy, poetically punctuated by the horror of the human condition. The connecting tissue between all three films is the dread of mortality, which in Beau is Afraid is given a run for its money by the terror of living.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: A truly original accomplishment that further cements Aster's reputation as a master of disquieting works of art.
reviews.author: Patrick Cremona

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid keeps pouring salt on an open wound. It revels in daring you to hate it. At least on that end, mission accomplished.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: There’s a lot to admire here, regardless. The performances are incredible, particularly Phoenix, who’s able to peek through Beau’s docile reserve to reveal a genuinely suffering soul. He injects the movie with the compassion the screenplay lacks.
reviews.author: Chad Byrnes

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid jumps all sharks.
reviews.author: Grant Rollings

reviews.text: Brilliant, perplexing, exhausting, indulgent, visionary. And yet Beau is Afraid will be hard work for some, particularly those who like neat and tidy endings.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: The revelations we do get are simplistic; rather than enrich the film, they stamp out any interpretive wiggle room.
reviews.author: Jorge Cotte

reviews.text: It’s not that the laughter is set against the despair. It is the despair itself that is so funny – so absurd, so pointless, so pathetic.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Some trips are worth the destination and, running a fully felt three hours, this film is one of them.
reviews.author: Matt Wolf

reviews.text: Genius filmmaker Ari Aster definitely knows how to push the audience's buttons, and his rambling, over-the-top movie is packed with moments that are hilarious, terrifying, riotously outrageous and darkly emotive.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: At just under three hours, Beau Is Afraid can be tough to stick with due to its tendency for self indulgence. That said, Aster remains a filmmaker with a singular vision, and a talent for poking at our inner most anxieties.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: It’s an anthology of unpleasantness.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: There are moments of extraordinarily absurd comedy, but the accumulation of all of them is not enough to hide the fact that what the director ultimately offers is a very uneven and paradoxically impersonal film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: There’s more than enough absurdist madness here to delight, infuriate and exasperate in equal measure.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: An impressive yet messy film.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: ... It’s like being cornered at a party by a moron who won’t stop describing this zany dream he’s just had, including the climactic appearance of a giant homicidal “penis monster”.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: But really the trick is on us, forced to endure Aster's self-indulgence in a film so long and loopy...
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Ari Aster goes off the rails with a self-indulgent three-hour freakout.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: An anxiety nightmare birthed onscreen, Beau is Afraid delights in its depravity, glistens with its absurdity, and overall entrances with Asters darkly horrific brand of humour.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: Aster’s film takes the so-traumatic-it’s-funny sequences of his previous work and spins them into a three-hour comedy of bad vibes and ritual humiliation. It’s as memorable, audacious, and indulgent as you’d hope from A24’s most expensive film to date.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: The movie is a chore, a grinding, faux-experimental folly from a company in the grip of a splattery midlife crisis. Would it not have been simpler just to get tattoos?
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: This film is probably not what Aster’s fans were expecting after a hiatus of almost four years, but I think it’s a wonderful take on Oedipal misery and the misery of drug abuse.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: …a vibrant, compassionate, alienating drama aimed specifically at giving you the absolute fear…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: It confronts us with the society in which we live, our bonds with mom and dad, sexuality, guilt, defenselessness, and much more. It is a failed heroic journey that raises questions that we rarely ask out loud [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Bond

reviews.text: The film ends in chaos, as the screenplay succumbs to its worst excesses.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Some viewers may leave feeling as if they've watched three pointless hours of someone's Freudian persecution fantasy. For others, though, the film will resonate as a powerful reminder that we are the ultimate origins of our guilt-ridden nightmares.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Watching Beau Is Afraid feels more like having the filmmaker himself sitting next to you, endlessly nudging you to make note of the thirty-seven tiresome production design curlicues he’s inserted into every single scene.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is another example of Aster’s ability to place you in an uncanny and occasionally uncomfortable environment, only to come out of the other side with the sense that you are the richer for it.
reviews.author: Andrew Gaudion

reviews.text: Aster has crafted a completely ridiculous and absurd film, and he’s fully in on the joke, even if the audience struggles with his particular brand and flavour of humour.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: I appreciate it for its craft, and that Joaquin Phoenix has some moments here that are exciting -- but he's a passenger in his own existence, and that's really boring.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: It’s pretty wild stuff, each individual sequence a testament to Aster’s determination to defy cliché by finding new ways to actively reflect the chaos the modern world.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: When everything is outlandish, nothing is. Beau Is Afraid should certainly be applauded for its originality and its confrontational tenor, but not its cartoonishly Freudian horror or the script’s meagre cod-psychology.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: Its authenticity and familiarity do not create a worthwhile viewing experience; even if its Oedipal and castration obsessions could be studied for years to come.
reviews.author: Callum Crumlish

reviews.text: Influenced all at once by the uneasy mental landscapes of Luis Buñuel, David Lynch and Charlie Kaufman, this is the guilt-tinged neurosis of every Jewish mamma’s boy writ large and rolled into one never-ending nightmare.
reviews.author: Anton Bitel

reviews.text: An exhilaratingly, mind-boggling examination of the act of not acting, acted beautifully.
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

reviews.text: Beau is Afraid is is a beautiful, juddering, picaresque voyage of discovery. A magnificent cine-soufflé best inhaled by a wide open mind to better savour the brain bending mayhem.
reviews.author: Daniel Goodwin

reviews.text: There's plenty to praise here, but even more feels half-baked or a bit too self-involved. At least Patti LuPone delivers the year's most surprising turn.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: ...is effective in putting you in this very intense nightmare/fantasy headspace where there are almost no interactions or exchanges that are imbued with compassion, or even moments of grace; everything is a full-on assault or the brief prelude to one.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: A wonderfully weird, polarizing film that stretches the outer limits of neurotic self-indulgence. It’s both too abstract yet packed with clunky metaphors and overt symbolism, but it strikes gold and finds success more often than not.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid  trips over itself during the climax. The film doesn’t necessarily need to be shorter — it’s just a long and expensive public therapy session with an overcomplicated script.
reviews.author: Kevin Fox Jr.

reviews.text: Whatever he’s working through with Beau Is Afraid, Aster’s unmistakable personal vision is on display and, refreshingly, leaves much to interpretation and much to be appreciated/
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The way Beau is Afraid indulges in itself as capital-A art reaches an inane point, turning whatever enjoyment you could get from its random developments into tedium, if not outright annoying.
reviews.author: Alton Williams

reviews.text: I was very happy that Beau never took his extreme anxiety POV to Costco at peak hours because I think watching something like that would've killed me.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: It is, undoubtedly, interesting, oppressive, and disruptive, but not as much as the director himself, who films with the arrogance of someone who is sure he has created a masterpiece, believes. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: Visually speaking, I think it’s Aster’s best work and overall Beau is Afraid will benefit from repeat viewings rather than just one sitting
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: It's a fever dream of a movie.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Phoenix delivers an outstanding performance in this hallucinatory and humorous nightmare that explores the inner traumas of a middle-aged man. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: ...an endeavor this bonkers has no business running a full three hours...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The kind of film you can’t get out of your head for days after experiencing.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: This, together with the surreal Oscar-blessed Everything Everywhere All At Once, represents for me the insurmountable quota for idiotic cinema intent on being original. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: Ari Aster proposes an Oedipal and Homeric journey into the most intimate and delirious mechanisms of fear. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: The absolute best part of “Beau Is Afraid” is doing the homework necessary to understand it. If that’s a turnoff, it makes total sense. But parsing the symbolism is the fun, if you’re so inclined.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: The movie is mean-spirited, deeply unpleasant and I laughed myself sick. Your mileage may vary.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: It’s difficult not to feel that there’s a better film lurking within that might have been rescued by a bit more red ink and a more ruthless re-think in the cutting room.
reviews.author: Tom Duggins

reviews.text: It's not a film about all the things that actually happen as much as it's a film about the feelings these events conjure up in us, the way they stir and poke at our own subconscious' terrors.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: The filmmaking in Beau is Afraid is amazing. There are very ambitious ideas going on. I just wish the three hour runtime was cut down some.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Unapologetic dark comedy and stellar performances save the film from being a complete three-hour slog of depressing events. Yet many viewers may leave the theater feeling drained and confused from the surrealist tragic-comedy.
reviews.author: Chauncey K. Robinson

reviews.text: Empty is this pedantic attempt to be Charlie Kaufman, a fearful, babbling misogynist tapestry, and Woody Allen's 'Take the money and run,' with a hipster myxomatosis. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text: Irreverent and poignant, relentless and restless. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Picatoste

reviews.text: In the end, a lot of the merit held by this exasperating therapeutic exercise is owed to [Joaquin] Pheonix's commitment.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: After two tightly scripted horror hits, Aster may now be lost in a web of quirky pretensions and indulgences, but that shouldn't stop audiences from savoring the mesmerizingly demented new design he's woven.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: Its paranoiac surrealism mutates from its most enticing feature into its greatest shortcoming during its three-hour runtime. That said, it’s clear that Aster is experimenting with his artistic vision, and it’s likely to produce excellence another time.
reviews.author: Maxwell Rabb

reviews.text: Daring and polemic, “Beau” is, if nothing else, a distinctive statement from a director who has no fear where it comes to plumbing the most disturbing human behavior and exposing it for the world to see.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Beau is Afraid is haunting, downright painful to watch, and will have you questioning your sanity. Despite that, the film is epic in scope, masterfully directed by Ari Aster and impossible to look away from.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: Overall, Beau Is Afraid works a lot more than it doesn’t, and it shows that Aster is truly a master of emotional storytelling and getting the best performances out of his actors.
reviews.author: Mey Rude

reviews.text: It starts out intriguing, great even, before spiraling into something bizarre and pointlessly bloated.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: This is the definition of a huge swing from Ari Aster. Joaquin mesmerizes, and the cinematography is phenomenal. The way this overlong nightmare is captured will engross viewers, but there are moments where the ridiculousness becomes too much.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Beau is Afraid is an out-of-the-box gallows comedy that is excruciatingly funny; a refreshing change of pace for writer/director Ari Aster that proves that horror and comedy can go together in perfect harmony.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Aster has instead dug deep into his own anxiety-ridden psyche to create something refreshingly new, different and entirely undefinable.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: The auteur has created a world filled with references, clues, and symbolisms, playing with the audience's expectations and constantly breaking the rules of narrative logic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: Along with being Ari Aster's most ambitious film, Beau Is Afraid is his funniest film in a twist, absurd way.
reviews.author: Caitlin Chappell

reviews.text: The filmmaker’s grand statement on anxiety in the modern age, as well as mothers and sons. One of the year's best movies, but certainly not for everyone.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Long, maddening, self-indulgent and kind of brilliant at the same time, it’s an auteur going for broke...
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: What elevates the film is its sense of style and comedy, coupled with a single-minded desire to depict anxiety-tinged madness.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is a surreal, sensory, and raw journey that doesn't leave behind a lesson, but plenty of disturbing questions. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Roberto Landaverde

reviews.text: This is a movie that will inspire deep love in some and seething hatred in others. But for most of us, Beau is Afraid will be, more than anything else, completely baffling.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: One has to question why Beau is Afraid exists at all.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Phoenix gives a rigor mortis performance.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: In a movie where the main character is a punching bag and every other character is lacing up their boxing gloves, there’s no human component with which I could relate. I choose to think that’s Aster’s failing, not mine.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Aster continues to be a visually masterful filmmaker. Unfortunately, he also continues his trend towards being overly indulgent and long-winded to once again comment on the themes of fear, guilt, and toxic relationships.
reviews.author: Cody Leach

reviews.text: Regardless of what you think is scaring Beau so much, he's still afraid, and we're still confused, but we enjoyed the ride enough to not fuss over the destination.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Ari Aster's "Synecdoche, New York."
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: There’s lots of moments to like, but it falls just short of greatness.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: With the Ari Aster touch,  the carnival of Beau’s journey adds a deeper layer, a cinematically farcical & necessary art to the whole Freudian battle. The casting reminded me of 1990s SPIN CITY – Nathan Lane! Richard Kind! Patti Lupone! Another Ari Wowsa!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is The Odyssey by way of the book of Job with a Cronenbergian reveal and Lynchian final scene, neither of which quite stick their landings.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: The thrilling and phantasmagoric Beau is Afraid shelves the horror. Instead, Aster confronts nice guy syndrome and the concept of a “mama’s boy” to critique 21st century culture.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is a bore, I’m afraid.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: I can respect the surreal approach and the broad scope of imagination, but the bloated running time destroys this movie.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Hilarious, oppressive, and confounding, Beau Is Afraid is an oedipal odyssey.
reviews.author: Chris Klimek

reviews.text: If Aster had simply chopped out the second of the film's three hours, it might have been more coherent, not less...
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: If you like mind-bending films that have unanswered questions at the end, middle and beginning, then you won’t be scared of Beau is Afraid.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: It might have been made to be screened at a psychoanalytical conference, with participants invited to submit papers.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: The story of the guy telling everybody not to applaud during the credits of Beau Is Afraid only gets funnier—and more profound—once you’ve seen it and can picture the precise backdrop of his plea.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: As confounding as Charlie Kaufman’s movies (like I'm Thinking Of Ending Things) can be, I never walk out of them feeling so bored and hollowed out like I did with Beau Is Afraid.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: Beau is a crazy, sometimes confounding, cinematic journey that most certainly won’t be for everyone, but if you do take the plunge, it’s a wild ride you won’t easily forget.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Not all of it works, and Beau never seems genuinely afraid at times others might hit the panic button, but Aster’s film, like his others, has that lingering provocative tease that’s both a sign and a gift.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: When the film does finally just come out and try to prod us into a big and overwhelming laugh, right at its climax, it lands with a thud, having worn everyone out so thoroughly that even something as ridiculous as the ultimate reveal is rendered limp.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: It’s a gifted filmmaker’s therapy session, and we’re paying for it.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: A shallow simulation of a magnum opus, filled mainly with flourishes but missing the vital spark of life that animates all its countless, superior inspirations.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid aspires to do no less than dramatize an American Psychiatric Association textbook’s worth of phobias and stressors — large, small, and yet-to-be-classified.
reviews.author: Andrew Dignan

reviews.text: It’s the narrative of every self-pitying boyfriend you’ve ever had, blown up to monumental proportions.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Phoenix’s committed performance displays a consistent and constant look of shock, yelling and whining throughout this comedy/horror film. It becomes not only predictable but repetitive played out over 3 very long hours.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: The trip will disturb audiences, alleviated by occasional comic spikes. Bold turns from Parker Posey, Amy Ryan and Nathan Lane lend dynamic support.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: It’s a hell of a thing– easily the wildest film you’re ever going to see on an IMAX screen– and proof that Aster is one of the most unique filmmakers working today.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: It's incredible. I'll never watch it again.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: A film with meticulously executed tonal command and emotional nuance.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: [I]t's vital to get on the wavelength immediately established by Ari Aster's epic psychodrama: Life for this character is a waking nightmare.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: "Beau Afraid" is one of the most unwatchable movies I’ve ever seen. It’s a death trap of ideas and a wasteland of talent. It’s an overlong bore that will have you craving antidepressants.  And Joaquin Phoenix isn’t going to save you or this movie.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Even Beau Is Afraid’s character portraits—usually a strength in Aster’s work—seem, despite the tumescent running time, strangely underdeveloped, even caricatural...it’s a surprisingly uninspired effort.
reviews.author: Leo Goldsmith

reviews.text: This ambitious and deeply introspective psychodrama about guilt, grief, and closure is unsettling, perplexing, and even disgusting. But its unique vision also is exhilarating, bolstered by an audacious portrayal from Joaquin Phoenix.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Madly, teemingly ambitious third feature... unabashedly Freud for thought, a full-bore, slow-tilt freakout, an interior mom-a-logue that advances as ponderous fable in distinct chunks, attenuated, animated, extenuated, exsanguinated.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: You’ll either love it or hate it as director Ari Aster tasks Joaquin Phoenix with his most challenging role as a total loser trying to get home to his mom (Patti LuPone). It’s not for everyone, except those starved for originality in copycat Hollywood.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: It must diminish its protagonist and distort the world in order to move the narrative forward, and all the ambition and sheer creativity isn’t enough to compensate for this core hollowness.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: “Beau is Afraid” is a skillfully constructed aberration with the ugliest worldview you can imagine.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: An epic odyssey that ultimately proves a grossly self-indulgent exercise in simplistic Freudian psycho-babble...a zonked-out “Mommy Dearest” tale revved up to absurd proportions and played as sour black comedy.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Beau is Afraid is a delicately crafted journey through both a physical and psychological labyrinth, whether audiences choose to make the journey with Beau or not remains to be seen.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: This movie is simply too bizarre to write off but not bizarre enough to truly inspire.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: Now honestly, this is a film I didn’t connect with in terms of story at all. Still, there is a strong handle of craft going on here with its filmmaking, and I can see it tackling its themes in interesting ways
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: It aims to illustrate the feeling of being a passive observer in a nightmare-fueled hellscape of an existence. And in that effort, it succeeds. I now know what it’s like to wish I can wake up from a film and forget it ever happened.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Whatever it is, Beau Is Afraid deserves not to be dismissed.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Rather than feel too much like an unloading of baggage, or, worse, fall into being tiresome cinematic therapy that is overly impressed with itself, Aster instead lets the credits roll over one final joke of a shot...
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Beau is Afraid is a Freudian nightmare come to life.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: I can’t say I enjoyed it much, but I was fascinated throughout, and that is saying something. A gonzo fantasia can be fun.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Going by this Occam’s Razor interpretation, the mere fact of this Caligulan pity party’s existence looks less like a showcase of narcissism and more a feat of creative individualism.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: What’s clear is that Aster remains a talented guy, though it would be clearer still if he weren’t so intent on throwing the talent in our faces. Over-compensation, perhaps.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: Ari Aster's Beau Is Afraid captures our collective social meltdown, even if it derails in the third act. Phoenix puts himself out there like never before. Parker Posey, too.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: There’s plenty going on beneath the surface, clues that a movie that is already surrealist enough, might be even more surreal than you can catch in one viewing.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: A movie that’s all talent and no discipline, which, in practice, is even worse than a movie that’s all discipline and no talent. At least the latter tries to please the audience; the former just pleases the filmmaker.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: It takes a certain level of patience to stick with Beau is Afraid all the way through, but those who do will be rewarded with an imaginative story that never stops being thought-provoking, even if you’re not entirely sure what Aster is trying to say.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: An enormously fun -- if also mind-boggling and head-spinning -- trip through his twisted subconscious.
reviews.author: Max Cea

reviews.text: Phoenix, for his part, exhibits characteristic dedication to what must be one of the more physically demanding characters he's taken on.
reviews.author: Keva York

reviews.text: Watching the movie feels disconcertingly like being unhappily drunk at a party whose guests are all old frenemies exchanging snippy, incomprehensible inside jokes you can only smile and nod at while trying to come up with an excuse to leave.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: The episodic nature of Beau's misadventures serves as both distraction and bloat, a metaphorical cavalcade that lacks the acerbic agility of many of its predecessor.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: Aster said he came up with this script before he developed his first two horror features, and indeed it feels like the work of a younger filmmaker who wants to say everything he can in this one story because he doesn’t know if he’ll get another chance.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: Never boring, but often frustrating, it’s the kind of $35 million auteurist Rorschach test that is destined for cult appreciation and years of contention.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: For all of Beau’s troubles, Phoenix is fantastic here. All the nervous energy that he knows how to harness for the sake of both dramatic and comedic results pays off in spades.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Do I like it? No, not at all. Is it art? Unquestionably, yes.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Each piece of Beau is Afraid teased out the same ideas repeatedly, shading in details, but never building to anything larger or more interesting than can be extrapolated from any single section.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: After crafting a demonic family disaster and a bonkers Swedish getaway, writer/director Ari Aster has concocted the mother of all guilt trips.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: It's pure, uncut Freudian spectacle: an epic of guilt and shame writ IMAX large, exorcizing familial demons on a bigger budget than A24 has ever shelled out.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: It’s depressing, at the end, to realize how much ado has been made about so little new.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Writer/director Ari Aster was wise to pursue Joaquin Phoenix as the paranoid protagonist of his Freudian odyssey of maternal Jewish guilt tripping, the actor the perfect victim of the filmmaker’s gleeful cinematic torture.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: It swings for the fences, burrowing in on its grandiose emotional ideas even if it often feels like a three-hour panic attack. Unpredictable, unexpected and ultimately, unexplainable, it’s challenging cinema that connects on a subconscious level.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Beau is Afraid is, without question, one of the best movies ever made about mental health. Hell, it might just be one of the best movies ever made.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Oedipus Complex: The Anxiety Comedy.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Beau is Afraid is a distinctive art piece full of idiosyncrasies and asides--it will not appeal to everyone, but those who resonate with it will find it endlessly fascinating.
reviews.author: Michelle Kisner

reviews.text: Cruelty and tedium, even with imaginative flair thrown in, doesn’t make for all that good a combination.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: It’s seldom meaningful, emerging as a feature only for Aster, who crafts quite the endurance test with “Beau is Afraid.”
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: "Beau is Afraid" is challenging, yes, but its reward is the way it uses art as a lightning rod. Love it or hate it, you're not going to forget it.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Aster pulls off the occasional little miracle here and there...
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: The sad truth is that, for all his ambition, cinematic prowess and hyper-confessional candor, Aster doesn't stick the landing.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Beau is Afraid is an overindulgent, disturbing, & hysterical mommy-issues movie that twists the hero's journey into an otherworldly contortion.
reviews.author: Graeme Guttmann

reviews.text: “Beau Is Afraid” ultimately left me cold.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Where to begin with Beau Is Afraid? The newest film from director Ari Aster is an overwhelming epic. A journey through the mind of an artist, crawling out the other end, and absorbing all his anxieties.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: It’s a film that, like “Midsommar” and “Hereditary,” rewards folks as they become more familiar with the inner trappings, and judging by the sheer lunacy Aster cooks up in some of these sequences, you’ll want to revisit this hellscape again and again.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: A surreal and anxiety-inducing odyssey through grief and guilt, Phoenix unsurprisingly shines with a forlorn performance, while Aster's nightmare-comedy succeeds more than falters.
reviews.author: Patrick Cavanaugh

reviews.text: ... to dismiss Beau’s horrors as humor renders the character meaningless... hoping for anything positive toward the protagonist will be punished swiftly and repeatedly for daring to care. The twist is Phoenix got paid to endure it... but audiences won’t.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: A long-haul onscreen psychotherapy session that leaves you with more questions than answers and dares you to take one of the year’s wildest, most provocatively daring movie rides.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is bold, enthralling, and unlike anything you've ever seen before. Whether that's a good or bad thing, well, Aster leaves how we enter this shrieking void up to the viewer.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: One of the strangest cinematic experiences you'll ever have, but also an extremely compelling and wryly comical one. It’s not really a movie made to be “liked.”
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: An epic black comedy that seeks to tease, titillate, confound, confuse and bewilder in equal measure. Think of it as an art movie adventure...It’s wildly unbalanced, as all good art is, veering from comedy to drama and back again, often in the one scene.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: To set up the movie’s cagey diminution of the protagonist, Aster diminishes the protagonist’s world, too—he suppresses Beau’s identity in the interest of stoking synthetic effects and inflating a hollow and shallow spectacle.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: If you are prepared for a big viewer commitment and relish those animated discussions afterwards (everyone will have a different bit to pick apart/comment on), then go. But also, be afraid, be very afraid.
reviews.author: Julian Wood

reviews.text: It’s a completely absurd movie with an incredible organizing principle that guides every twist and every oddity toward an utterly relatable allegory about anxiety and how (Jewish) mothers can pass that down.
reviews.author: Jason Flatt

reviews.text: Yes. Beau Is Afraid is entertaining, confusing, confounding, and emotional – you can apply many descriptive adjectives
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: Aster has not only re-confirmed his status as a unique voice in contemporary American cinema, he’s also established himself as a chronicler of the disintegration of the modern American family in particular and relationships in general.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid takes a long road to not get very far. That could, of course, be the point. But the simpering sad sack Beau -- despite Phoenix’s typically committed and sympathetic performance -- remains curiously void, stuck in a one-note nightmare.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: If you ever played the dungeon crawler video game The Binding of Isaac and wanted a Charlie Kaufman-like film adaptation, Beau Is Afraid is for you.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: A three-hour-long panic attack in psychosomatic cinematic form... will have you upping your meds the minute you leave the theater. A Thunderdome of maternal disappointment!
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is not a movie for everyone – actually, it is a movie for very, very, very few. But I just happen to be part of that teeny tiny target audience. And for me, Beau Is Afraid kills.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: A kaleidoscope of genres, BEAU IS AFRAID quite the journey.
reviews.author: Norman Gidney

reviews.text: Nothing in director Ari Aster's previous movies can prepare viewers for what awaits them in this strange, unsettling, surreal, experimental epic with a deep-dive performance by Joaquin Phoenix.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: A bleak film that unloads some 'elevated horror' on us.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: It’s bold, it’s unhinged, and while it may not be as rewatchable as his previous two films, it’s certainly unforgettable.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is an experimental fever dream about parent/child issues and mortality. Ari Aster fans expecting a horror movie will be disappointed. Joaquin Phoenix's acting is stellar, but this three-hour film is too long and too weird for some viewers.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Does Aster think we’re too slow, or too dumb, to pick up hints as we go? Some viewers will revel in such excess; I found it ever more wearisome...
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is abrasive and dense, but that’s to be saluted. Aster is cashing in on the success of his first two films to create something daringly vulnerable for a wide audience.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: There are two main positives here: the cast filled with wonderful supporting actors, and the production design, particularly in the fabulous forest-set theatrical sequence. However, Aster is not as shocking, funny, or thought-provoking as he thinks he is.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: It’s important to remember that Beau Is Afraid is not a puzzle to be solved or a mystery to be unlocked. That’s by design.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: A bold, provocative and surreal portrait of an adult child of a malignant narcissist. Joaquin Phoenix gives one of the best performances of his career.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Like a drug cocktail that the heavily medicated Beau might take, the movie energizes but ultimately enervates.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: It's as easy to admire the incredible artistic effort that went into the film as it is to never want to watch it ever again.
reviews.author: Reuben Baron

reviews.text: This movie is three hours long, and almost every minute of its home stretch might have been custom-designed to crush a viewer’s interest. (And it’s not a fun horror movie, by the way.)
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid offers arresting confirmation of Aster’s talent and fresh evidence of his limitations.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: A bleak Oedipal nightmare that throbs like a migraine for three lost hours.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: [Ari Aster] digs so deep in the well he's invited us to drink from so much that in the end, can't find his way out. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: What if “Taxi Driver” was remade as a Kafkaesque dark comedy? What if the crushing neurosis of Woody Allen and his oedipal comedies were reframed as emotionally traumatic horror movies?
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: The film is at its best when Aster is unafraid to spill his emotional guts, so to speak, without care for how others will react to it.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Aster’s voice is strong and Beau certainly feels like part of his oeuvre even as he expands the definition of what that really means. The only way to truly know what to make of it is to see it.
reviews.author: Sarah Gorr

reviews.text: It is tough to care about a mouse who matters so much less to the filmmaker than the shiny mousetrap where he’s imprisoned you both.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: It’s an extraordinary and deliciously demented study of a tortured soul of clumped memories.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: With Beau Is Afraid, his third and easily most ambitious feature to date, Ari Aster traces, to more cosmic and absurd ends, how tragedy is birthed by, well, birth itself.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid cements Ari Aster as one of the most fascinating big screen storytellers working today.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: It’s not an entirely unpleasant journey, but the film does have a jarring, unfinished feel to it...
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: It’s a brain-melting, deeply harrowing, existentially idiosyncratic complex portrait of a son and mother with a black comedy heart that transcends genre classification
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid feels like being pinned down by your sleep paralysis demon while it crouches on your chest and screams dick jokes at you.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: Exactly what we have come to expect from Aster, this movie is utterly bizarre with a third act that goes completely off the rails. It is impossible to look away from Joaquin Phoenix, who delivers one of his best performances here.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: What began as a comically exaggerated paranoid farce ends as an audacious slice of surreal, Charlie Kaufman-esque purgatorial art, likely to draw admirers as much as a sense of alienation.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: It’s too early to say whether this is Aster’s best film. Still, it’s certainly his most ambitious, using the tools of terror he’s cultivated thus far to eke existential horror out of more universal humanistic impulses.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: Fascinating, but will turn off a mainstream audience.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Did you ever hear the one about the boy who feared his mother? “Beau Is Afraid” tells this joke for three gobsmacking, sometimes exhausting, always beguiling hours.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: Aster’s most divisive effort yet, but those willing to ride the wave of genre and mind-bending insanity will find themselves rewarded by a profoundly imaginative Kafkaesque odyssey as dementedly funny as it is often horrifying.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: [A] bad movie where every few scenes you have to admit that what’s happening right now kinda rules.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: That Aster has even got a film this wilfully perverse made is miraculous. Violent, hallucinogenic, twisted – there are not enough adjectives to even scratch the surface of this hugely ambitious psychological drama ... A once-in-a-generation kind of movie.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: I can't promise you'll enjoy Beau is Afraid. I can promise it'll f*ck you up.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: You have to respect Ari Aster for getting Beau is Afraid produced and out into the world. That's different than enjoying the film, which is befuddling, massively unenjoyable, and three hours of my life that I'll never get back.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: There is an objective story to Beau is Afraid, but also a metaphor that can provoke analysis and conversations long after the three-hour epic. Either aspect is a worthwhile experience. and those who engage in both will be exponentially rewarded.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: I’d love to say I love it as more than a filmmaker taking a massive swing with the full support of a studio, but I can’t. It left me feeling upset and exhausted, which I think was the goal, but it’s a journey I’m not entirely sure I needed to take.
reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid hates Beau, no doubt, but it hates his mother, too, and it hates everyone who shows him both kindness and cruelty, a comedy of neither manners nor errors.
reviews.author: Fran Hoepfner

reviews.text: A true American original, and proof that, while the hype surrounding [Aster] may have been early, it wasn’t wrong.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is an epic odyssey through the peculiar and the macabre that delights itself in its own never-ending tank of anxiety.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Even as it’s spiraling in its final moments, and raising more questions than it ever feels interested in answering, there’s a mesmerizing, captivating quality to it all that makes it hard not to get drawn into the strangeness of Aster’s vision.
reviews.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore

reviews.text: While incredibly overwhelming, Ari Aster’s BEAU IS AFRAID is a sweeping epic that perfectly encapsulates anxiety in all its forms.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: Though this may share a certain anything-goes absurdity and deliriousness with another recent A24 hit, the fact that the studio has now given us that Oscar-winner’s evil twin is itself a riotous hoot. This is the anti-Everything Everywhere All at Once.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: It’s the most magnificent act of oversharing you’ll see all year, a banquet of all the TMI you can eat, just for the price of a ticket. Though when you think about it, shouldn’t Aster be paying us?
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: It’s a gonzo odyssey for our times, a rejection of mediocre cinema, and a paean for all the perverted weirdos out there. This one’s for you, sickos.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: A sickly picaresque guilt trip that stretches a single Jewish man’s swollen neuroses into a three-hour nightmare so queasy and personal that sitting through it feels like being a guest at your own bris (in a fun way!).
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Running at over three hours, Beau Is Afraid is a colossal recovered memory of mock Oedipal agony which is scary, boring and sad in approximate proportions of 1 to 4 to 2.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: The kind of movie you can take bets on which is the first scene that will cause mass walkouts. Those who stay will find much to chew on and, perhaps, to scratch their heads about.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: If the character invites more cringing pity than emotional investment, that’s more to do with the distancing effect of Aster’s surreal approach than anything lacking in Phoenix’s raw, gaping wound of a characterization.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is big, declarative cinema. Irksome (or worse) as some of the film may be, it has a gravitational pull. I stayed seated in the dark, pressed into my chair, until the end credits were done rolling.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: ... The film’s cumulative unmanageableness soon starts to look like a put-on – Aster seems much more interested in pushing the limits of his audience, rather than his own.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: As [Beau is Afraid] drags on into its second and then third hour, you just feel like you’re being punk’d, and Ari Aster is getting the last (and only) laugh.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: It makes sense that Aster would make his third film a sprawling epic after the head rush of initial acclaim. It’s admirable that it’s disarming, strange and deeply unserious...It also all pretty much works.
reviews.author: Brianna Zigler

reviews.text: Part gorgeous nightmare fuel, part comedic odyssey, the unrelenting trip into the higher consciousness of a 40-something man is an astounding pillar of artistic genius.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: At points, it’s a stress-watch to rival the Safdie bros' nerve-shredder Uncut Gems. But it’s also a deeply funny Freudian head-shag, laden with Jewish guilt and unresolved mummy issues.
reviews.author: Jordan Farley

reviews.text: A Freudian hellride.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: There will surely be a small contingent who embrace this as their new favorite movie, but three hours doesn’t feel at all reasonable for such an uneven collection of sketches.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Beau Is Afraid is unlike anything Aster has created. It’s a mammoth miracle of a movie that he could only make after the success of his first two films.
reviews.author: Sophia Ciminello

reviews.text: “Beau Is Afraid” may not be a horror film in the same sense as “Hereditary” and “Midsommar,” but it’s a different kind of horror, one that will challenge, alienate and push people out of their comfort zones.
reviews.author: Matt Neglia

reviews.text: Worth recommending for its ambition alone, merely to witness the audacious result of anxious self-loathing writ large across the silver screen, without an ounce of restraint. That it’s also a remarkably well-crafted horror-comedy is a cherry on top.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: 'Beau Is Afraid' is Ari Aster at his most free and his most unhinged.
reviews.author: Mary Beth McAndrews

reviews.text: In Beau is Afraid, Beau is the world and the world is Beau, and as he sloshes around in the turmoil of his own subconscious, you may recognize yourself in his many fears.
reviews.author: Julia Glassman

synopsis: A paranoid man embarks on an epic odyssey to get home to his mother in this bold and ingeniously depraved new film from writer/director Ari Aster.
